references.text: Description of the composition of the anointing oil and its use to consecrate priests and holy objects.
Moses carries out what is commanded in Exodus 29:21 by sprinkling anointing oil and blood on Aaron, his sons, and their garments.
Sprinkling of blood seven times as part of the purification ritual, parallel to the sprinkling in the consecration ceremony.
Description of the holy garments for Aaron and his sons that were to be consecrated through sprinkling.
First mention of the use of anointing oil on Aaron's head during the consecration process.
Command to anoint Aaron and his sons for priestly service, linking to the consecration in 29:21.
The high priest who is anointed with oil and consecrated to wear the holy garments.
The book of Hebrews refers to blood sprinkling as necessary for purification and consecration under the old covenant.
Complements the ritual with instructions regarding the inheritance of the holy garments.
The general instruction that the specific action in the source verse fulfills.
